An Average Japanese Meal
May 2022 • Couples
This restaurant comes across as having been around for a long time and is a popular haunt by locals. We had a late lunch and as a result, grilled dishes were not available. We ordered a set lunch which included an assortment of sashimi, assortment of tempura, rice, soup, and we added chawanmushi, deep fried squid head and lime tea. It’s odd that a Japanese restaurant did not offer green tea or roasted barley tea on its beverage menu. The serving was generous and food tasted good. But the tempura did not appear like tempura. Rather, it looked like they used the wrong batter. Price is reasonable and taste is good. But not very authentic Japanese looking food, if you asked me. Although, I understand the owner is a Japanese!

Old Zen charms
Jan 2020 • Friends
Japanese food is aplenty in Saigon but Zen is more than a household name. Though its my first time having lunch there, I can certainly appreciate why it is one of my Viet friend's favourite haunt. The sashimi is super fresh and the yakitori sticks are perfectly grilled without being charred. The side dishes of cold somen and miso soup were exceptionally tasty without the usual heavy saltiness of soy and miso. Delicious and unpretentious traditional Japanese food coupled with the warm ambience and friendly service makes it a worthwhile Japanese food choice when visiting Saigon.

Excellent & authentic - try this if you have time for 1 jap restaurant in HCMC
Dec 2017 • Couples
The title sounds like a misnomer - Jap food in HCMC? Yes, you bet. The famour Le Than Ton street is like a mini Tokyo, frequented by Jap expats. You will find the street lined with many jap joints and bars. I have tried most of these and would say that Zen Saigon stands out as the best. 

Don't expect a fine-dining setting, this is a homely restaurant serving great authentic Jap food. I usually make it a point to revisit a great restaurant before returning from a holiday, and I did just that for this restaurant - Dinner and Lunch. 

They also have private tatami rooms and a quaint bar area. Try the sushi set, all sets come with a dessert at the end.

Excellent Yakitori
Oct 2016 • Solo
Zen Saigon Japanese restaurant has the best yakitori in Saigon. If I am correct the ownership originally had the Nanbantei of Tokyo franchise, which was in a much more attractive building than the current location of Zen. The location is on popular Le Thanh Ton Street, where there are numerous restaurants, all a short walk from the hotels around Lam Son Square.

While the menu has a fairly large variety of Japanese food, I only come for the yakitori, which has a set course or a la carte. The menu has all the Nanbantei favorites, such as Asparagus Maki, Shisho Maki, Gingo Nuts, Tsukune and Shitake mushrooms.

Zen is popular with the Japanese expat community in Saigon, so reservations at dinner are a must. Often, failing to make reservations, I end up eating at the bar, which is okay as the beer in nearby. Service is good and the yakitori prices are reasonable.
